title: Improv troupe turns audience ideas into a Nov. 14 fundraiser at Uptown
summary: Better Than Bacon Improv headlines Comedy for a Cause at Uptown Knauer Performing Arts Center on Saturday, Nov. 14 at 7:30 p.m., with musical comedian Todd Chappelle opening. Proceeds from the show, wine grab and silent auction go to the Coatesville Youth Initiative and Brandywine Valley Active Aging; tickets are $31 for members and $36 otherwise.

title: Hometown Christmas Parade returns Dec. 4 with more marching bands
summary: The Greater West Chester Chamber of Commerce's free parade runs Friday, Dec. 4, rain or shine, starting with the tree lighting at 6:30 p.m. and the procession at 7. This year's lineup adds marching bands by popular demand, works in an America250 tribute and ends with Santa.

title: Refill shop opens on East Street Road for soap, pasta and skincare by the ounce
summary: West Chester Refillery Station, which held its grand opening Oct. 24 at 54 E. Street Road near the new Goodwill, sells household and personal-care products in bulk: bring or buy a container, weigh it, fill it and pay only for the product. The husband-and-wife owners say many shoppers come in to buy just enough to try something.

title: WCU's Ram Poll finds economy and health care top of mind for state system students
summary: West Chester University faculty surveyed 550 undergraduates across all 10 PASSHE universities ahead of the midterms. The economy and health care each ranked among the top three issues for 45 percent of students and education for 42 percent, while fewer than half said they were confident the election would be free and fair.

title: History Center lights up for a monthlong Season of Lights starting Dec. 2
summary: The Chester County History Center fills its galleries with illuminated displays and decorated trees from Dec. 2 through Jan. 2, open Wednesday through Saturday, 10 a.m. to 4 p.m., and closed Dec. 25 and Jan. 1. The exhibit is included with regular admission: $10 adults, $7 seniors, $5 children and students.
loc: Chester County History Center, 225 N. High St., West Chester

title: Tree Commission launches a self-guided Tree Trail through the borough
summary: The West Chester Tree Trail is a walking tour of 11 notable trees or tree groups chosen to show off the borough's canopy, its history and its variety, timed for fall color. The tour takes an hour or two; pamphlets are at Borough Hall or on the borough website.
loc: Borough Hall, 401 E. Gay St., West Chester

title: Christmas Tree Train returns to the West Chester Railroad on three Sundays
summary: The two-hour excursion leaves Market Street Station at 8 a.m. on Nov. 29, Dec. 6 and Dec. 13 for Wiggins Tree Farm, where riders cut their own tree and crews load it on a flatcar for the trip back. Hot chocolate and donuts are sold on board.

title: Borough seeks volunteers for seven boards, applications due Dec. 4
summary: Borough Council is taking resumes for seats on the rail service committee, Historical Commission, Human Relations Commission, Library Board, Recreation Commission, Transportation Advisory Committee and Tree Commission. Applicants email a resume to the borough by Dec. 4 and will be scheduled for interviews.
loc: Borough Hall, 401 E. Gay St., West Chester

title: Clover Market brings 125 vendors to Westtown School Nov. 21-22
summary: The fourth annual Clover Market Holiday Market fills Westtown School's Athletic Center with makers and vintage sellers from 10 a.m. to 4 p.m. both days. Admission and parking are free, with food trucks outside.

title: Borough still hunting the source of odors in southeastern neighborhoods
summary: Residents near the Goose Creek Treatment Plant began reporting unpleasant smells in mid-October, and the borough says staff are still working to pin down the source, though the plant is operating within its permit. Anyone who notices something unusual is asked to call the plant at 610-696-2320.
loc: Goose Creek Treatment Plant, West Chester
